newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Six confirmed dead in Dutch Dakota crash.
newsitem.headline: Six confirmed dead in Dutch Dakota crash.

text.p: Six people were confirmed dead and one person was badly injured after a DC-3 Dakota carrying 26 passengers and six crew plunged into the North Sea near the Dutch naval town of Den Helder on Wednesday, the coastguard said.
"Six bodies have been recovered and one person has been transferred to hospital," coastguard spokesman Gerrit Miedema told Dutch radio.

Dutch news agency ANP earlier reported that at least 10 people had died. It reported sightings of apparently lifeless bodies still strapped into their seats, drifting in the water near the crash site.
A navy spokesman said the 55-year-old vintage propellor-powered plane was operated by the Dutch Dakota association and had been on a sightseeing flight over the Netherlands.
A spokesman for the association declined to comment on whether it was their Dakota which had crashed.
"We don't have any information yet. We will be holding a news conference later," he said.
